newsitem.title: CANADA: Big Chinese newspaper launches Canada edition.
newsitem.headline: Big Chinese newspaper launches Canada edition.

text.p: One of China's biggest newspapers launched a Canadian edition Friday as part of a growing effort to reach an overseas audience.

Officials from Shanghai-based Xin Min Evening News and the Chinese government signed a distribution agreement for the newspaper with a Canadian company at a ceremony in Vancouver. The paper is expected to sell a few thousand copies a day in Canada at first.

Founded in 1929, the daily paper has a circulation of 1.8 million in China and is the largest evening newspaper in the country, officials said. Xin Min is owned and operated by the government. Xin Min started a Chinese-language U.S. edition
last year. The paper's general managing editor, Fu Ming Yun, said Xin Min decided to branch into Canada because it wanted to reach Canada's large population of Chinese immigrants.

"Canada and China enjoy very good relations. (The launch of) Xin Min here will further enhance our mutual understanding," Song You Ming, China's consul general in Vancouver, told the signing ceremony.

The paper will open a reporting bureau in Vancouver, which has a large Chinese community. Several Chinese-language newspapers are already published in the city, including offshoots of large Hong Kong and Taiwanese papers.

Media analysts said Xin Min's move overseas may reflect a desire to present China's perspective on events to overseas Chinese. The newspaper is also seeking to make money by selling advertisements in the U.S. and Canadian editions.
